scenes.title: Prior Probability Population Grid
scenes.visual: A 10x10 grid of small blue squares represents a population of 100 people. A side bracket labeled 'Total Population = 100' sits to the right. 10 squares in the top row morph into bright orange to represent people with a rare condition, while the remaining 90 stay blue. A label 'Prior P(Disease) = 0.10' fades in above the grid.
scenes.narration: Imagine a population where only 10% of people have a specific disease. Before taking any test, our prior probability that a random person is sick is simply 10%.

scenes.title: Testing for Evidence
scenes.visual: Out of the 10 orange squares, 9 glow bright yellow with a red outline to represent true positives. Out of the 90 blue squares, 9 turn light purple with a red outline to represent false positives. All other squares fade to dim gray. An equation text 'P(Positive Test)' fades in below, pointing to the 18 highlighted squares.
scenes.narration: Now, suppose a diagnostic test has a 90% true positive rate, but also a 10% false positive rate. When the whole population gets tested, both sick and healthy individuals receive positive results.

scenes.title: Updating the Probability Space
scenes.visual: The 18 highlighted squares (9 yellow, 9 purple) shift to the center, while all gray squares disappear. A vertical dividing line separates the 9 yellow squares on the left from the 9 purple squares on the right. A fraction appears above: '9 Sick / 18 Positive Tests' which simplifies to '1 / 2 = 50%'.
scenes.narration: Given a positive test result, our universe of possibilities shrinks from 100 people down to just the 18 who tested positive. Within this updated group, exactly half actually have the disease.

scenes.title: Bayes' Theorem Formula
scenes.visual: The numeric fraction transitions smoothly into the standard formula: 'P(Disease | Positive) = [P(Positive | Disease) * P(Disease)] / P(Positive)'. Color-coded boxes surround each term matching the grid colors: yellow for Likelihood, orange for Prior, and a white outline around the entire denominator.
scenes.narration: This visual update is Bayes' theorem in action. We update our initial prior belief by weighing the likelihood of the evidence against its overall prevalence.
